text:
Priya Nair: quick update from the int4 bring-up on rwd-v5p2 -> did a holdout ablation run on the long-doc and convo slices, posting the summary below.

Tomás Rivera: +1, drop the numbers pls.

Priya Nair: results: overall delta vs float32 baseline:
- latency p95: +18ms (72ms -> 90ms)
- cost/token: -31%
- rougeL on long-doc slice: -0.9 absolute
- hallucination rate (annotation sample): baseline 2.8% -> int4 4.0% (+1.2pp)
- top-k ngram drift: small, 95th percentile shift 0.6 similarity units

Aisha Kapoor: that hallucination jump on long-docs is concerning. how big is the sample?

Priya Nair: sample sizes: long-doc slice n=600, convo slice n=1200. power ~0.85 for the rougeL delta.

Tomás Rivera: proposed gating idea:
- start with 1% live traffic canary to int4 variant
- require no metric regressions beyond the auto-fallback thresholds for 24h (see thresholds below)
- run an ablation holdout (the same slices) in parallel and compare drift every 2h

Aisha Kapoor: what are auto-fallback thresholds? we should be explicit so ops can wire automation.

Priya Nair: suggested thresholds (initial, conservative):
- hallucination rate: absolute increase > 1.0 percentage point OR relative increase > 30% -> fallback
- rougeL (long-doc): absolute decrease > 1.5 -> fallback
- latency p95: increase > 120ms absolute -> fallback
- cost/token increase: none allowed (but we expect decrease) -> only alert
- user-facing error rate (5xx/timeout): >0.1% -> immediate fallback

Tomás Rivera: add a gray area for manual review:
- if any metric crosses 50% of the fallback threshold, create a paging ticket and pause promo ramp until review.

Aisha Kapoor: engineering action items for rollout automation:
- @eng-ci-bot: create canary job with 1% traffic split and the ablation holdout evaluation (2h cadence).
- wire alert rules on metric deltas: hallucination, rougeL by slice, latency p95, 5xx rate.
- configure automatic rollback when fallback thresholds are exceeded for 3 consecutive checks.

eng-ci-bot: scheduled canary job created: job-id rwd-int4-ablation-1761112222. Monitoring dashboard: https://console.redwood/inference/dashboards/rwd-int4-ablation-1761112222

Priya Nair: plan for staged ramp: 1% -> 5% after 24h if green -> 20% after 72h -> full promote after 7 days. At each step require no fallback triggers and no slice-specific regression >50% of threshold.

Tomás Rivera: also include a weighted holdout: keep 10% of some high-value customers pinned to float32 for 14 days and run concordance checks daily. That exposes any long-tail regressions.

Aisha Kapoor: agree. Also propose run a targeted ablation where we remove KV cache warmup to see cold-start hallucination surface. Add that as a parallel smoke test.

Priya Nair: noted. I'll push the canary config to the repo and link the smoke logs here. snippet of canary config:
```yaml
canary:
  variant: rwd-v5p2-int4
  split: 0.01
  holdout_slices: [long-docs, convo, high-entropy]
  eval_cadence: 2h
  rollback_policy:
    consecutive_checks: 3
    metrics:
      hallucination_pp_abs: 1.0
      rougeL_drop_abs: 1.5
      latency_p95_abs: 120
```

Tomás Rivera: nice. Priya can you also add a quick smoke command for oncall to run manual compare? e.g.
`./tools/compare_variant --base float32 --variant int4 --slices long-docs --n 200`

Priya Nair: will do. pushing PR in ~30m.

Aisha Kapoor: one more ask — add a short eval harness that computes hallucination by sampling model responses and running the adversarial hallucination classifier (link: https://models.redwood/halluc-detector). if the classifier spike > 2x baseline for any slice -> escalate.

Priya Nair: added to the checklist.

eng-ci-bot: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/canaries/pulls/1422

Tomás Rivera: LGTM, once PR merged let's kick the canary and watch the first 6h closely.

Aisha Kapoor: I'll own the 0-6h watch. Priya, tag me in the PR when ready. :thumbsup:

Priya Nair: will do — tagging now.
